_comment: Planning-versus-execution classifier rules (file name is historical). Ordered: the first matching rule wins for a run. Edit words here, not in code; the dashboard re-reads this file (plus phases.local.json beside project.json, whose entries run first) and the rules hash in API payloads changes, invalidating caches. Only labels are ever read, never prompts or argv.

rules.comment: Explicit convention wins: ws9-plan-xxx, ws9-exec-xxx, ws9-review-xxx, ws9-coord-xxx (dashes, dots, underscores and spaces all count).
Dashboard tooling lanes attributed to a workstream (harness, composer) are coordination, even when they carry -fix/-rev suffixes.

Structural review marks: an r- lead (review rounds), a -rev/-fix/-check tail (verify iterations), or a -rev- infix (ws9-rev-s-itemkey). Checked before task mapping so a review pass over a task counts as review.

A run mapped to a plan task id is execution: exact taskmap keys, /regex/ taskmap keys, the WS1/WS2/WS7 page matchers, plan-id substrings, and the generic ws<N>-<slug> form (ws9-s-tbench names plan task WS9.s-tbench).
Planning words: scoping and design work before and around the build.
Review words: verification passes over built work. 'diff' (comparing marts) and 'check' read as verification; task-mapped diff lanes already matched above.
Doing words: building, shipping and operating the pipeline.
Coordination words: status and sync traffic, not build work.
An unmapped lead session (no parent run, a lead source) is the planning surface: the hub thinking, not a task lane. Task-mapped and keyword runs already matched above.
Still unclassified and started before the workstream's first task-mapped run: early exploration belongs to planning.
